experiment.plan: Arm every live collector on Core and the Minion, run for five 300 s collection cycles, then finalize. Fleet held at 14,250 devices, the failing rung of the 300-thread search at max-repetitions 5: Core CPU about 90%, 36 old-generation collections per 15 min, GC 22% of wall time, the pending queue running away past 13,900. netem delay 75ms 25ms on netsim enp6s19. This is the failing state before the Core is resized to 32 GiB / 20 GiB heap. GC logging was enabled at runtime with jcmd VM.log because neither JVM is started with -Xlog, so the GC logs are pulled separately from /var/tmp/gclog.
experiment.question: What are Core and the Minion actually doing over five collection cycles at the CPU-and-heap ceiling, 14,250 devices with 50-100 ms per SNMP PDU, max-repetitions 5 and 300 threads?

host.cpu: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E5-2650 v4 @ 2.20GHz, 8 cores

sut.config_delta:
One change against the pool-200 search. Everything else is identical.

OpenNMS Core, snmp-config (Config Manager, rest/cm/snmp-config/default)
  definition max-repetitions="5" for range 10.42.0.0 to 10.42.255.255
  root unchanged: version v2c, read-community public, timeout 1800, retry 1, max-vars-per-pdu 10, max-repetitions 2
  the file etc/snmp-config.xml is ignored on this release; the CM copy is authoritative
  verified on the wire: N=0 M=5 on every table GETBULK, 58 requests and 4.4 s per collection (149 and 11.5 s at the default)

OpenNMS Core, unchanged from the pool-200 search
  collectd-configuration.xml: threads 300, thresholding-enabled false on every service
  opennms.conf: JAVA_HEAP_SIZE 10240, JAVA_INITIAL_HEAP_SIZE 8192, -XX:+UseG1GC, -XX:NativeMemoryTracking=summary; MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=4 via systemd drop-in
  opennms.conf: OPENNMS_DATABASE_CONNECTION_MAXPOOL and MAXSIZE 250, MINPOOL 25
  opennms.conf: 13 daemons disabled (Pollerd, Bsmd, Ticketer, Correlator, Queued,
                Actiond, Notifd, Scriptd, Rtcd, SnmpPoller, EnhancedLinkd, Statsd,
                Ackd, PerspectivePoller); Syslogd enabled
  org.opennms.features.kafka.producer.cfg: forward.metrics true, metricTopic metrics
  org.opennms.core.ipc.strategy kafka; org.opennms.timeseries.strategy osgi, no store
  provisiond and datacollection: no file on disk, compiled-in defaults

simulator, netsim-benchmark-01, unchanged
  tc qdisc netem delay 75ms 25ms on enp6s19, uniform 50 to 100 ms per packet, responses only

PostgreSQL, unchanged
  conf.d/10-benchmark-tuning.conf, pgtune web profile for 16 GiB / 8 vCPU
  max_connections 400, shared_buffers 3997MB, effective_cache_size 11993MB

Capture notes: GC logging enabled at runtime with jcmd VM.log (gc.log pulled by hand under hosts/*/jvm/*/). Window ran 40 min instead of 26 because the scheduled stop was delayed by macOS throttling a background sleep on the workstation; both hosts' Kafka-side pcap rings (Core enp6s20 at 32 GB, Minion enp6s19 at 3 GB) wrapped and hold the end of the window. The capture's per-minute jcmd snapshots force a full GC via the class histogram; the first five minutes show a compacted heap. This is the failing rung before the Core resize to 32 GiB / 20 GiB heap.
